_about: Every word the player reads. {n} and the like are filled in by the core.
title: Graftwood
subtitle: Grow a creature from what you defeat. An auto-battling roguelike in the woods.
description: A 3D auto-battling roguelike: walk a branching path through the woods, fight bugs, crustaceans and woodland creatures, and graft their body parts onto your own.
no_webgl: This browser has no WebGL 2, so the woods cannot be drawn. The game still plays; the picture is missing.
how: Your creature has mass: one body part fits on each unit of it. You start with 3.
Drag parts onto your creature to graft them, into your bag to keep them for later (up to 2; they do nothing there), or into the bin.
Every part with a timer acts when its timer runs out. Fights play themselves; your build decides them.
Win a fight and either raise your max health or take one of the loser's parts. Forage too: a full forage bar cultivates a unit of mass.
Every creature and part is a Bug, Rodent, Beast or Critter. Two or more parts of one kind earn a set bonus. Wild parts suit any creature.
Encounters on the path are half good and half bad. Some add mass or upgrade a part; some take mass, and a part that no longer fits falls off.
Past 5 mass, each extra unit of mass and each extra part slows all your parts by 10%.
One evasion is one percent to dodge an attack. Poison stacks to 10; each stack deals 1 damage every 2 seconds. Regeneration heals at most 3 a second.
choose_hint: Each starts with 3 mass and 2 parts, so there is room for one more. Once you are in the woods, drag parts on and off your creature.
map_hint: Pick where to go next. The Old Stag waits at the end.
